sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor’s degree must be completed before enrollment; a mathematics degree is recommended, with
advanced coursework/research/teaching helpful. Central guidance requires at least a B average in the last two
undergraduate years. International applicants are eligible. [s1] [s4] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select the doctoral route and submit only ONE application in the admission cycle; simultaneous applications to
multiple UCSC departments are not accepted. Register referees at least two weeks before the deadline. If
requesting a mathematics fee waiver, prepare and upload the separate financial-need statement. [s1] [s3] [s8]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Program contact: mathgradadvising@ucsc.edu. The department encourages familiarity with its research and
can coordinate visits, but does not pre-assess applications. A mandatory adviser agreement was not found. [s1]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Only one application per cycle. Central instructions say no edits after submission; mathematics says no
changes after the application close date, so complete and proofread before submission and ask about any
needed correction. Check the portal for letter and document receipt. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s8]
Cycle verification [Unresolved]
Fall 2027 applications are open, but the exact mathematics deadline and current test-policy table remain
unresolved. Several public pages retain older-cycle language. [s5] [s8] [s9] [s10] [s11]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Mathematics admission minimums fall under the general category: old TOEFL 83/new 4.0, or IELTS 7. TA
eligibility separately requires TOEFL speaking 26/new 5.0 or IELTS speaking 8. Scores expire after two years
and must be electronic. DET and Versant are not accepted. IELTS One Skill Retake language still contains a
stale 2024 postponement, so current acceptance needs confirmation. [s4] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Applicants who have completed a four-year English-medium bachelor’s may request an admission waiver in
the English Proficiency section, specifying a backup test method/date. Waivers are decided only when
admission is recommended, not beforehand; in-progress UChicago degree treatment is not explicit. The
separate TA waiver ordinarily requires a US master’s plus TA experience, final transcript, and supervisor
verification. A UChicago bachelor’s alone does not meet that published TA waiver route. [s4] [s5]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Unresolved for Fall 2027. The old 2025-26 department page says GRE scores are not required; the current
catalog still lists GRE, particularly the subject test, among admission factors. The current central
program-by-program test table was not retrievable. Obtain current written confirmation rather than treating
either old statement as controlling. [s5] [s9] [s10]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three required; up to five allowed. Electronic PDF upload or typed/pasted text; qualitative assessment rankings
are optional for the writer. No emailed or faxed letters. [s3] [s4]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
This specific reference detail was not established by the public program/graduate application instructions
checked. Confirm it in the current referee-help screen or with admissions before entering contacts; no
invitation was triggered during research. [s1] [s3] [s4]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
After entering details and choosing FERPA access, click Send To Recommender; that sends the secure link.
Registration is recommended at least two weeks before the deadline. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations can be sent before final application submission; the application can be submitted before all letters
arrive, but they remain subject to the program deadline. [s3] [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The submitted application checklist displays letter status. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Conflict]
A submitted letter cannot simply be replaced online; the recommender can contact Graduate Admissions from
the registered email to arrange a new letter. Letter services are accepted using unique addresses. To change
FERPA selection, the FAQ says exclude and re-register the referee, which removes the prior letter; the how-to
page calls the selection irreversible. Reuse across cycles is not established. [s3] [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
No exact annual mathematics stipend was established. A 50% TA appointment is 220 hours per quarter,
approximately 20 hours/week. Central guidance warns ordinary TA tuition remission excludes nonresident
supplemental tuition unless another award covers it; obtain explicit NRST coverage in the offer. UC Article 35,
Table B.1, sets the Group 1 quarter-system 50% TA salary at USD 4,278/month at point 1 from October 1, 2027
(points 2/3: 4,449/4,582). UCSC and UCR fall in Group 1. Nine paid months at point 1 would total USD 38,502
by arithmetic; this is a negotiated wage scale, not a verified mathematics annual package, funded-month
promise, net stipend or summer guarantee. Confirm appointment fraction, starting point, dates and
supplements in the offer. [s1] [s7] [ucwages2027]
Years of support [Standing rule]
PhD support is guaranteed for five years under the department’s conditions; a sixth year is usually supported
with satisfactory progress. Support beyond year six requires discussion at the start of that year and should not
be expected. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students can receive support, but TA oral-English eligibility and nonresident supplemental
tuition coverage must be checked separately. F-1 applicants should not assume federal FAFSA aid eligibility.
[s1] [s5] [s7]
Conditions and duties [Unresolved]
TA/GSR duties, satisfactory progress, enrollment, and offer terms apply. Summer support must be read
separately; no universal summer stipend was established. [s1] [s7]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
This particular funding term was not established by the public program/admissions material checked. Obtain
the exact rule in the funding offer or from the graduate coordinator; neither eligibility nor a guaranteed
amount/duration is inferred from silence. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Central examples include Chancellor fellowship funding and an annual housing supplement for eligible full-time
doctoral students. These are not verified universal mathematics awards, and exact 2027 amounts/citizenship
criteria were not established. [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 155 international; USD 135 domestic. Nonrefundable and not deferrable. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
International applicants cannot use the central need waiver, but mathematics offers 30 need-based waivers
per cycle. Upload the ≤500-word financial-need statement. Published international workflow: answer No to
needing fee assistance and Yes to program payment, submit without paying despite the card message, then

email mathgradadvising@ucsc.edu. This is a request, not approval; prior recipients receive lower priority. [s1]
[s4]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor’s degree must be completed before enrollment; a mathematics degree is recommended, with
advanced coursework/research/teaching helpful. Central guidance requires at least a B average in the last two
undergraduate years. International applicants are eligible. [s1] [s4] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select the doctoral route and submit only ONE application in the admission cycle; simultaneous applications to
multiple UCSC departments are not accepted. Register referees at least two weeks before the deadline. If
requesting a mathematics fee waiver, prepare and upload the separate financial-need statement. [s1] [s3] [s8]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Program contact: mathgradadvising@ucsc.edu. The department encourages familiarity with its research and
can coordinate visits, but does not pre-assess applications. A mandatory adviser agreement was not found. [s1]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Only one application per cycle. Central instructions say no edits after submission; mathematics says no
changes after the application close date, so complete and proofread before submission and ask about any
needed correction. Check the portal for letter and document receipt. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s8]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor’s degree must be completed before enrollment; a mathematics degree is recommended, with
advanced coursework/research/teaching helpful. Central guidance requires at least a B average in the last two
undergraduate years. International applicants are eligible. [s1] [s4] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select the doctoral route and submit only ONE application in the admission cycle; simultaneous applications to
multiple UCSC departments are not accepted. Register referees at least two weeks before the deadline. If
requesting a mathematics fee waiver, prepare and upload the separate financial-need statement. [s1] [s3] [s8]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Program contact: mathgradadvising@ucsc.edu. The department encourages familiarity with its research and
can coordinate visits, but does not pre-assess applications. A mandatory adviser agreement was not found. [s1]
Portal workflow [Conflict]

changes after the application close date, so complete and proofread before submission and ask about any
needed correction. Check the portal for letter and document receipt. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s8]

Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
No exact annual mathematics stipend was established. A 50% TA appointment is 220 hours per quarter,
approximately 20 hours/week. Central guidance warns ordinary TA tuition remission excludes nonresident
supplemental tuition unless another award covers it; obtain explicit NRST coverage in the offer. UC Article 35,
Table B.1, sets the Group 1 quarter-system 50% TA salary at USD 4,278/month at point 1 from October 1, 2027
